<a id="cwyapi"></a>

## `CwyApi`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Mods.CwyApi` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

The version of the CWY:LS Mod Loader mod API: the one number a manifest's `loaderVersion` is checked against, for content packs and code mods alike.

SemVer. Until [`CwyApi.FreezeVersion`](#cwyapi--freezeversion) (CWY:LS Mod Loader 1.0) the API is 0.x: a minor version may change or remove members, and every such change first ships a [`CwyDeprecatedAttribute`](#cwydeprecatedattribute) notice. From 1.0 on a breaking change needs a new major version; deprecated members stay until then.

The BepInEx plugin version of CwyLs.ModLoader is this same string, so the startup line, the `version` command and the manifest check can never disagree.

<a id="cwyapi--freezeversiontext"></a>

### `const string FreezeVersionText = "1.0.0"`

The version at which the API freezes (SemVer 1.0.0).

<a id="cwyapi--pluginversiontext"></a>

### `const string PluginVersionText = "0.9.1"`

The API version as a compile-time constant, for attribute arguments such as the framework's own `[BepInPlugin]`. A mod must not use it: a constant is copied into the mod when it is compiled, so it would keep reporting the version the mod was built against. Read [`CwyApi.Version`](#cwyapi--version) (or [`CwyApi.VersionText`](#cwyapi--versiontext)) at run time instead.

<a id="cwyapi--versiontext"></a>

### `static readonly string VersionText`

The running API version as text. `static readonly`, not a constant, so a mod reads the version of the framework it runs on, not the one it was compiled against.

<a id="cwyapi--freezeversion"></a>

### `static SemVer FreezeVersion { get; }`

The version at which the API freezes, parsed.

<a id="cwyapi--isfrozen"></a>

### `static bool IsFrozen { get; }`

True once the API has reached [`CwyApi.FreezeVersion`](#cwyapi--freezeversion): after that, only a major version may break a mod.

<a id="cwyapi--version"></a>

The API version, parsed.

<a id="cwyapi--satisfies"></a>

### `static bool Satisfies(SemVer minimum)`

True when a manifest asking for `minimum` can load on this API. Null (no `loaderVersion`) is always satisfied.

**Parameters**

- `minimum`: The manifest's `loaderVersion`.

## `CwyDeprecatedAttribute`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Mods.CwyDeprecatedAttribute` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Base: `Attribute`

Marks a member of the mod API as deprecated. The attribute documents the decision; the member's body calls the framework's deprecation notifier, which writes one line per calling mod per session at [`CwyDeprecatedAttribute.Stage`](#cwydeprecatedattribute--stage).

**Example**

```csharp
[CwyDeprecated("0.9.0", DeprecationStage.Info, Replacement = "helper.Satone.Say")]
public static void SayLegacy(string text)
{
    CwyDeprecations.Notify("SayLegacy", "0.9.0", DeprecationStage.Info, "helper.Satone.Say");
    ...
}
```

<a id="cwydeprecatedattribute--ctor"></a>

Marks a member as deprecated.

**Parameters**

- `since`: The API version that deprecated it, e.g. `0.9.0`.
- `stage`: How loudly it announces itself.

<a id="cwydeprecatedattribute--replacement"></a>

What to use instead, for the log line; null when there is no direct replacement.

<a id="deprecatedmembers"></a>

## `DeprecatedMembers`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Mods.DeprecatedMembers` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Finds the [`CwyDeprecatedAttribute`](#cwydeprecatedattribute) that governs a running method. `MethodBase.GetCurrentMethod()` inside a deprecated property is `get_X`, inside an event `add_X`, inside an interface implementation the class's method - none of which carries the attribute the author put on the property, the event or the interface member. The search order: the member itself; an accessor's property or event; the interface members it implements (and their property or event); then the declaring type and the interfaces. Results are cached per member; thread-safe.

<a id="deprecatedmembers--find"></a>

### `static DeprecatedMemberInfo Find(MemberInfo member)`

The deprecation that governs `member`, or null when there is none.

**Parameters**

- `member`: A member, typically `MethodBase.GetCurrentMethod()` inside the deprecated one.

**Returns:** The attribute and the name to report; null when nothing is deprecated.

<a id="deprecationstage"></a>

## `DeprecationStage`

enum · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Mods.DeprecationStage` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

How loudly a deprecated member announces itself, after SMAPI's deprecation levels. Each mod that calls the member gets one line per session, at this level.

| Name | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| <a id="deprecationstage--notice"></a>`Notice` | 0 | Will not be removed soon. The line goes to the trace file only, so players never see it; mod authors find it there. |
| <a id="deprecationstage--info"></a>`Info` | 1 | A console line at normal level: authors should move off it in their next update. |
| <a id="deprecationstage--pendingremoval"></a>`PendingRemoval` | 2 | Will be removed at the next breaking version (a 0.x minor before 1.0, a major after): a console warning. |

## `HotkeyClaims`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Mods.HotkeyClaims` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

The rules the hotkey registry applies when a feature or a mod claims an id and chords. Pure; the Unity-side registry (`CwyLs.ModLoader.Input.Hotkeys`) only maps its bindings onto these. An owner is the config file the keys are bound in (its path), so every mod is its own owner and the framework's features share one.

<a id="hotkeyclaims--modconfigsection"></a>

### `const string ModConfigSection = "Hotkeys"`

The config section a mod's hotkeys are bound in, inside the mod's own .cfg.

<a id="hotkeyclaims--modidprefix"></a>

### `const string ModIdPrefix = "mod:"`

Prefix of a mod hotkey's registry id: `mod:<modId>/<key>`.

<a id="hotkeyclaims--clashes"></a>

### `static IReadOnlyList<string> Clashes(string id, HotkeyChord primary, HotkeyChord alternate, IEnumerable<HotkeyInfo> others)`

The other bindings that already use one of these chords, e.g. `console.toggle (Ctrl+Shift+C)`. A clash is a warning, not a refusal: both keys fire, and the player can rebind either. Unset chords never clash.

**Parameters**

- `id`: The id being registered; its own binding is skipped.
- `primary`: Its primary chord.
- `alternate`: Its alternate chord.
- `others`: Every registered binding.

**Returns:** One entry per clashing binding and chord, in registry order. Never null.

<a id="hotkeyclaims--configslot"></a>

### `static void ConfigSlot(string id, string frameworkSection, out string section, out string key)`

Where a hotkey's two chords live in its owner's config file. A mod hotkey (`mod:<modId>/<key>`) is bound in the mod's own .cfg as section [`HotkeyClaims.ModConfigSection`](#hotkeyclaims--modconfigsection), key `<key>` - the mod id is the file already. Any other id keeps `frameworkSection` and the id itself.

**Parameters**

- `id`: The registry id.
- `frameworkSection`: The section for framework keys, e.g. `Keys`.
- `section`: The config section.
- `key`: The config key prefix (the registry adds `.Primary` and `.Alt`).

<a id="hotkeyclaims--decide"></a>

### `static HotkeyClaim Decide(string id, string owner, IEnumerable<KeyValuePair<string, string>> held, out string holder)`

Decides what registering `id` for `owner` means.

**Parameters**

- `id`: The id being registered.
- `owner`: Who registers it (a config file path).
- `held`: Every registered id with its owner.
- `holder`: The owner that holds the id, or null when nobody does.

**Returns:** The verdict.

<a id="modassemblyresolver"></a>

## `ModAssemblyResolver`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Mods.ModAssemblyResolver` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

The order the framework's `AssemblyResolve` handler answers in: an already-loaded assembly of that simple name for anyone; then, for a requester that is a mod, its own folder and the other mod folders in load order; for an unknown requester, a mod folder only when exactly one has the name; for anyone else, never a mod folder. Shared names and other mods' entry names are never served from a mod folder. Mono does not probe a mod's folder for its private dependencies, so without this they do not load at all. Pure: the file system is a callback.

<a id="modassemblyresolver--decide"></a>

### `static ModAssemblyDecision Decide(string requestedName, ModAssemblyRequester requester, string requesterFolder, ModAssemblyEnvironment environment)`

Decides where a requested assembly comes from.

**Parameters**

- `requestedName`: The full name the runtime asked for, e.g. `MyLib, Version=1.0.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=null`.
- `requester`: Who asked.
- `requesterFolder`: For [`ModAssemblyRequester.Mod`](#modassemblyrequester--mod), the folder of that mod's entry DLL; otherwise ignored.
- `environment`: What is loaded and where the mod folders are.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentNullException`: `environment` is null.

<a id="modassemblyresolver--samefolder"></a>

True when two folder paths name the same folder (case-insensitive, trailing separators ignored).

**Parameters**

<a id="modassemblyrules"></a>

## `ModAssemblyRules`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Mods.ModAssemblyRules` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Assembly-identity rules for code mods: one copy of every shared assembly per process. A mod may ship private helper DLLs, but a copy of something the game, BepInEx or the framework provides is never loaded from a mod folder - two copies of one identity give "`MyType` cannot be cast to `MyType`", and HarmonyX cross-wires the patches of two copies of one build.

<a id="modassemblyrules--sharedfamilies"></a>

### `static readonly IReadOnlyList<string> SharedFamilies`

Name families that are always shared, whether or not an assembly of that name is loaded yet: the framework, the game, Unity, BepInEx, Harmony, MonoMod, Cecil and the core runtime. A name matches a family when it equals it or continues it with `.` or `-`.

`System` and `Microsoft` are not whole families. A provider SDK needs `System.ClientModel`, `Microsoft.Extensions.*` or `System.Collections.Immutable`, which the game does not ship; the ones it does ship (`System.dll`, `System.Text.Json`, `Microsoft.Bcl.AsyncInterfaces`, ...) are shared because they are in its `Managed` folder or already loaded - the loader passes those as the known-shared list.

<a id="modassemblyrules--findbundledreserved"></a>

### `static IReadOnlyList<KeyValuePair<string, string>> FindBundledReserved(IEnumerable<string> packFiles, string entryDll, string ownModId, IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> reservedNameOwners)`

The DLLs in a mod folder that are another code mod's entry DLL. Every planned mod's entry assembly name is reserved to that mod's own folder, so such a copy is never loaded - otherwise it would load first and the real mod would be refused as [`ModSkipReason.AssemblyAlreadyLoaded`](#modskipreason--assemblyalreadyloaded). The loader warns the bundling mod.

**Parameters**

- `packFiles`: The bundling mod's files, relative to its root.
- `entryDll`: Its own normalised entry DLL path, excluded from the check.
- `ownModId`: Its id; names it reserves itself are not reported.
- `reservedNameOwners`: Entry assembly simple name → the id of the mod that owns it. Case-insensitive lookups.

**Returns:** (relative path, owning mod id) pairs, sorted by path; empty when there are none. Never null.

<a id="modassemblyrules--findbundledshared"></a>

### `static IReadOnlyList<string> FindBundledShared(IEnumerable<string> packFiles, string entryDll, ICollection<string> knownShared)`

The DLLs in a mod folder (other than its entry DLL) that are shared assemblies. They are never loaded - the resolver serves the process's own copy - so the loader only warns.

**Parameters**

- `packFiles`: The pack's files, relative to its root.
- `entryDll`: The normalised entry DLL path, excluded from the check.
- `knownShared`: Shared names beyond [`ModAssemblyRules.SharedFamilies`](#modassemblyrules--sharedfamilies); null for none.

**Returns:** The offending relative paths, sorted; empty when the folder is clean. Never null.

<a id="modassemblyrules--findsamebuild"></a>

### `static string FindSameBuild(Guid mvid, IEnumerable<KeyValuePair<string, Guid>> loaded)`

The name of an already-loaded assembly with the same module version id (the same build, perhaps renamed), or null. HarmonyX keys patch methods by MVID, so two copies of one build would run each other's patches.

**Parameters**

- `mvid`: The new assembly's manifest-module MVID.
- `loaded`: Name and MVID of every other loaded assembly.

<a id="modassemblyrules--isalreadyloaded"></a>

### `static bool IsAlreadyLoaded(string simpleName, IEnumerable<string> loadedSimpleNames)`

True when an assembly named `simpleName` is already loaded, which means loading the entry DLL would hand back that one or load a second copy. Refused as [`ModSkipReason.AssemblyAlreadyLoaded`](#modskipreason--assemblyalreadyloaded).

**Parameters**

- `simpleName`: The entry DLL's simple name, from its metadata.
- `loadedSimpleNames`: Simple names of every assembly loaded in the process.

<a id="modassemblyrules--isshared"></a>

### `static bool IsShared(string simpleName, ICollection<string> knownShared)`

True when `simpleName` is shared: in one of the [`ModAssemblyRules.SharedFamilies`](#modassemblyrules--sharedfamilies), or in `knownShared` (names loaded now, or shipped in the game's Managed folder, BepInEx's core folder or the plugins folder).

**Parameters**

- `simpleName`: An assembly's simple name, e.g. `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`.
- `knownShared`: Further shared names; null for none.

<a id="modconsolelines"></a>

## `ModConsoleLines`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Mods.ModConsoleLines` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Console tags and the startup summary line of the code-mod loader. Pure, so the wording is unit-tested.

Two tags, both one word: [`ModConsoleLines.ModsTag`](#modconsolelines--modstag) for what the framework says about mods (loaded, skipped, failed, deprecated calls) and [`ModConsoleLines.ModTag`](#modconsolelines--modtag) for what a mod says itself through its helper's log. The tags live in [`ConsoleTags`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Logging.md#consoletags) ([`ConsoleTags.Mods`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Logging.md#consoletags--mods), [`ConsoleTags.Mod`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Logging.md#consoletags--mod)); the two constants here are aliases so existing call sites stay valid.

<a id="modconsolelines--loadersystem"></a>

### `const string LoaderSystem = "mods"`

Bus `sys` of the loader's events.

<a id="modconsolelines--modstag"></a>

### `const string ModsTag = "MODS"`

The loader's tag: `MODS` (alias of [`ConsoleTags.Mods`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Logging.md#consoletags--mods)).

<a id="modconsolelines--modsystem"></a>

### `const string ModSystem = "mod"`

Bus `sys` of a mod's own log lines; the bus event name is the mod id.

<a id="modconsolelines--modtag"></a>

### `const string ModTag = "MOD"`

A mod's own log lines: `MOD` (alias of [`ConsoleTags.Mod`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Logging.md#consoletags--mod)).

<a id="modconsolelines--failure"></a>

### `static string Failure(string modId, ModStage stage, string label, string errorType, string message, int suppressed)`

The primary column of a failure line: `cwy.sample.hello failed in Entry: NullReferenceException: …`.

**Parameters**

- `modId`: The mod.
- `stage`: Where.
- `label`: Which handler or command, or null.
- `errorType`: The exception's type name.
- `message`: The exception's message.
- `suppressed`: Repeats swallowed since the last line for this site.

<a id="modconsolelines--oneline"></a>

### `static string OneLine(string text)`

Collapses line breaks so an exception message cannot break the one-line grammar.

**Parameters**

- `text`: Any text.

<a id="modconsolelines--summary"></a>

### `static string Summary(IReadOnlyList<ModStatus> statuses)`

The primary column of the one summary line after loading: `1 loaded (cwy.sample.hello@0.1.0); 1 skipped (x.mod: NoEntryType); 0 failed`. Lists are omitted when empty, like the pack summary; the tag column already says MODS, so the text does not repeat it.

**Parameters**

- `statuses`: Every code mod's outcome, in load order.

<a id="moddatakey"></a>

## `ModDataKey`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Mods.ModDataKey` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Names of the files a mod keeps in its own data folder (`BepInEx/data/mods/<id>/`). A key is the file name: letters, digits, `_`, `.` and `-`, 1 to 64 characters, not starting with a dot. That keeps every key a plain file in that one folder on both operating systems, with no way to reach a path outside it.

<a id="moddatakey--pattern"></a>

### `const string Pattern = "^[A-Za-z0-9_-][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$"`

The key rule, as a human-readable pattern.

<a id="moddatakey--tempsuffix"></a>

### `const string TempSuffix = ".tmp~"`

Suffix of the file an atomic write goes to before it replaces the real one. Contains a character a key cannot, so it never collides with a key.

<a id="moddatakey--isvalid"></a>

### `static bool IsValid(string key)`

True when `key` is a usable data file name.

**Parameters**

- `key`: The candidate.

<a id="moddatakey--require"></a>

### `static void Require(string key)`

Throws unless `key` is valid, naming the rule.

**Parameters**

- `key`: The candidate.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentException`: The key breaks the rule.

<a id="moddatakey--tempname"></a>

### `static string TempName(string key)`

The temporary file name an atomic write of `key` uses.

**Parameters**

- `key`: A valid key.

## `ModExceptions`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Mods.ModExceptions` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Turns the exceptions the runtime wraps around a mod's own error back into that error, and reads the assembly names out of type-load failures. Pure; unit-tested.

<a id="modexceptions--missingassemblies"></a>

### `static IReadOnlyList<string> MissingAssemblies(IEnumerable<Exception> loaderExceptions)`

The simple names of the assemblies a set of loader exceptions could not find: the `FileName` of a `FileNotFoundException`/`FileLoadException`, else a name quoted in the message. Distinct, in first-seen order.

**Parameters**

- `loaderExceptions`: The `ReflectionTypeLoadException.LoaderExceptions`; null entries are skipped.

**Returns:** The names. Never null.

<a id="modexceptions--typeloadhint"></a>

### `static string TypeLoadHint(IReadOnlyList<string> missingAssemblies, IReadOnlyList<string> optionalDependenciesNotRunning)`

The explanation at the end of the loader's "N type(s) could not load" warning. It names the likely cause instead of always blaming a CWY:LS Mod Loader version: an optional dependency that is not running, a missing private DLL, or a framework mismatch.

**Parameters**

- `missingAssemblies`: From [`ModExceptions.MissingAssemblies`](#modexceptions--missingassemblies).
- `optionalDependenciesNotRunning`: Ids of this mod's optional dependencies that are not installed or did not load.

**Returns:** One sentence fragment, starting lowercase, no trailing period.

<a id="modexceptions--unwrap"></a>

### `static Exception Unwrap(Exception error)`

The exception the author wants to see: reflection wraps constructor and invoke failures in `TargetInvocationException`, and a throwing static constructor surfaces as `TypeInitializationException`. Both are peeled, repeatedly.

**Parameters**

- `error`: What was caught.

**Returns:** The innermost mod exception; `error` itself when nothing wraps it.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentNullException`: `error` is null.

<a id="modfailurelimiter"></a>

## `ModFailureLimiter`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Mods.ModFailureLimiter` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Keeps a mod that throws on every frame from burying the log: the first failure at a site is logged, repeats within [`ModFailureLimiter.WindowSeconds`](#modfailurelimiter--windowseconds) are counted silently, and the next logged line carries that count. Thread-safe; pure logic over a caller-supplied clock.

A site is a bounded key ([`ModFailureLimiter.SiteKey`](#modfailurelimiter--sitekey): owner, stage and the first word of the label), and the table holds at most [`ModFailureLimiter.MaxSites`](#modfailurelimiter--maxsites) of them, so labels that carry data (`chunk 17`, a file path) can neither defeat the limit nor grow the table without end.

<a id="modfailurelimiter--ctor"></a>

### `ModFailureLimiter(double windowSeconds = 10.0, int maxSites = 256)`

Creates a limiter.

**Parameters**

- `windowSeconds`: How long after a logged failure repeats stay quiet. At least 0.
- `maxSites`: Most sites tracked at once; at least 1.

<a id="modfailurelimiter--defaultmaxsites"></a>

### `const int DefaultMaxSites = 256`

Default most sites tracked at once.

<a id="modfailurelimiter--labelkeylength"></a>

### `const int LabelKeyLength = 24`

The longest label prefix a [`ModFailureLimiter.SiteKey`](#modfailurelimiter--sitekey) keeps.

<a id="modfailurelimiter--overflowsite"></a>

### `const string OverflowSite = "(other sites)"`

The site every failure shares once the table is full of sites still in their window.

<a id="modfailurelimiter--maxsites"></a>

### `int MaxSites { get; }`

Most sites tracked at once (the overflow site not counted).

<a id="modfailurelimiter--pendingsuppressed"></a>

### `int PendingSuppressed { get; }`

Total failures swallowed across every site since the last logged line of each.

<a id="modfailurelimiter--sitecount"></a>

### `int SiteCount { get; }`

Sites currently tracked, the overflow site included.

<a id="modfailurelimiter--windowseconds"></a>

### `double WindowSeconds { get; }`

Seconds after a logged failure during which repeats are only counted.

<a id="modfailurelimiter--labelkey"></a>

### `static string LabelKey(string label)`

The first word of a label, bounded; see [`ModFailureLimiter.SiteKey`](#modfailurelimiter--sitekey).

**Parameters**

- `label`: A label, or null.

**Returns:** The prefix; empty for null.

<a id="modfailurelimiter--shouldlog"></a>

### `bool ShouldLog(string site, double nowSeconds, out int suppressed)`

Records one failure and decides whether to log it.

**Parameters**

- `site`: Where it happened, normally a [`ModFailureLimiter.SiteKey`](#modfailurelimiter--sitekey), e.g. `cwy.sample.hello|Event|RoomReady`.
- `nowSeconds`: A monotonic clock.
- `suppressed`: How many repeats were swallowed since the last logged line.

**Returns:** True when this failure should be logged.

<a id="modfailurelimiter--sitekey"></a>

### `static string SiteKey(string owner, string stage, string label)`

The bounded site key for a failure: `owner|stage|labelKey`, where the label key is the label up to its first space, digit, quote, colon, bracket or slash, at most [`ModFailureLimiter.LabelKeyLength`](#modfailurelimiter--labelkeylength) characters. `chunk 17` and `chunk 18` share a site.

**Parameters**

- `owner`: Who: a mod id or a dispatcher owner.
- `stage`: Where: a stage name, or a short word such as `tick`.
- `label`: Which handler or work item; null for none.

**Returns:** The key. Never null.

<a id="modskipreason"></a>

## `ModSkipReason`

enum · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Mods.ModSkipReason` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Why the loader refused a code mod that the pack resolver had accepted. The resolver's own reasons (a missing `entryDll` file, a framework that is too old, a missing dependency) are [`PackSkipReason`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Packs.md#packskipreason)s; these are the ones only known once the assembly is in hand. Numbered explicitly so the values stay stable.

| Name | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| <a id="modskipreason--noentrytype"></a>`NoEntryType` | 0 | The assembly has no concrete class deriving from `CwyMod` with a parameterless constructor. |
| <a id="modskipreason--multipleentrytypes"></a>`MultipleEntryTypes` | 1 | The assembly has more than one concrete `CwyMod` class, so the entry is ambiguous. |
| <a id="modskipreason--assemblyloadfailed"></a>`AssemblyLoadFailed` | 2 | The assembly could not be read or loaded (bad image, missing file, I/O error). |
| <a id="modskipreason--assemblyalreadyloaded"></a>`AssemblyAlreadyLoaded` | 3 | An assembly with the entry DLL's name, or the same build under another name (same MVID), is already loaded: two copies of the mod, or a name clash. A second copy would cross-wire Harmony patches, so it is never used. |
| <a id="modskipreason--dependencyfailed"></a>`DependencyFailed` | 4 | A required code-mod dependency was skipped or failed at load time. |
| <a id="modskipreason--disabled"></a>`Disabled` | 5 | Code mods are switched off (`[Mods] Enabled=false`). |
